title: Restrict CORS allowed origins in SecurityConfig
body:
### Current Issue
In `SecurityConfig.java` (line 67), the configuration `config.setAllowedOrigins(List.of("*"))` allows any domain to make cross-origin requests to the API.

### Impact
In a production environment, this misconfiguration exposes the application to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) and data exfiltration attacks from any malicious website.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Replace the wildcard `*` with specific trusted frontend origins.
- Ensure external frontend clients can still connect.
- Validate that requests from unauthorized origins are rejected with CORS errors.

title: Remove hardcoded PostgreSQL password from docker-compose
body:
### Current Issue
The database password (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 123andi123`) is hardcoded in plain text on line 6 of `docker-compose.yml`.

### Impact
Committing plain-text credentials to the repository is a severe security vulnerability. Anyone with repository access can read the database password.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Replace the hardcoded password with an environment variable reference (e.g., `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}`).
- Create a `.env.example` file documenting the required variables.
- Verify the application still connects to the database successfully using the `.env` file.

title: Remove default password fallback from application.yml
body:
### Current Issue
In `application.yml` (line 13), the datasource password is configured as `password: ${DB_PASSWORD:123andi123}`. If the `DB_PASSWORD` environment variable is not set, the real password is used as the default.

### Impact
A misconfigured deployment (missing env var) silently uses a known password, creating a security vulnerability that is hard to detect.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Remove the default value: change to `password: ${DB_PASSWORD}` with no fallback.
- Ensure the application fails to start if `DB_PASSWORD` is not set.
- Document the required environment variable in deployment docs.

title: Protect shared routine endpoint with rate limiting and secure tokens
body:
### Current Issue
In `SecurityConfig.java` (line 34), the path `/assigned-routines/shared/**` is in `permitAll()`. In `AssignedRoutineService.java` (line 155), the share URL is generated using `UUID.randomUUID()`, which is predictable with enough information.

### Impact
An attacker can brute-force UUID v4 tokens to access other users' assigned routines without authentication.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Replace `UUID.randomUUID()` with cryptographically secure tokens (e.g., `SecureRandom` + `MessageDigest` or `TokenGenerator`).
- Add rate limiting to the shared endpoint (e.g., max 10 requests per minute per IP).
- Return 429 Too Many Requests when the limit is exceeded.

title: Implement rate limiting for authentication endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
The login endpoint `/auth/login` in `AuthController.java` (line 18) does not have rate limiting applied. Only the AI endpoint has protection via `RateLimiterService`.

### Impact
An attacker can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing attempts without being blocked.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Apply rate limiting to `/auth/login` (e.g., max 5 attempts per minute per IP or email).
- Return `429 Too Many Requests` status code when the limit is exceeded.
- Add integration tests to verify the rate limiter blocks excessive requests.

title: Enforce stronger password validation on registration
body:
### Current Issue
In `RegisterRequest.java` (line 8), the password validation only requires `@Size(min = 6)`. No uppercase, numbers, or special characters are enforced.

### Impact
Weak passwords are trivially guessable, increasing the risk of account compromise through credential stuffing or brute-force attacks.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add validation rules: at least one uppercase letter, one digit, and one special character.
- Return a clear error message when the password does not meet requirements.
- Update any existing tests that register with weak passwords.

title: Implement proper JWT refresh token mechanism
body:
### Current Issue
In `AuthController.java` (line 24), the `/auth/refresh` endpoint requires a valid authentication token. This is not a true refresh token — it should use a separate token with a longer expiration.

### Impact
Users must re-authenticate when the access token expires, degrading UX. A separate refresh token improves security by allowing short-lived access tokens.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Implement a refresh token (separate JWT with longer expiration) returned alongside the access token on login/register.
- Create a `/auth/refresh` endpoint that accepts only the refresh token.
- Invalidate the refresh token after use (rotation) or on logout.
- Store refresh tokens (or their hashes) in the database for revocation support.

title: Implement JWT token blacklist for logout and revocation
body:
### Current Issue
In `JwtService.java`, there is no blacklist mechanism. If a token is compromised, it remains valid until expiration.

### Impact
Compromised or stolen tokens cannot be revoked. Users have no way to log out or invalidate sessions.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Implement a token blacklist (Redis or database table) for revoked tokens.
- Add a `/auth/logout` endpoint that blacklists the current token.
- Check the blacklist in `JwtAuthFilter` before accepting a token.
- Set an appropriate TTL on blacklist entries matching token expiration.

title: Stop exposing raw Student entities in SyncPullResponse
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncPullResponse.java` (line 10), the `students` field is typed as `List<Student>`, returning raw JPA entities directly as HTTP response. This exposes internal fields like `trainer_id` and other fields not intended for external consumption.

### Impact
Leaking internal model data exposes sensitive information. It also causes potential lazy initialization exceptions and couples the API response to the database schema.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Replace `List<Student>` with a dedicated DTO (e.g., `StudentResponse`).
- Ensure the DTO only exposes fields necessary for the client.
- Update `SyncService.toAssignedResponse()` and related mapping code accordingly.

title: Add validation annotations to SyncPushRequest
body:
### Current Issue
`SyncPushRequest.java` has no `@Valid` annotations. The `operations` list field accepts null or an unbounded array.

### Impact
An attacker can send an extremely large array of operations in a single request, causing memory exhaustion and denial of service.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@NotNull` and `@Size(max = 100)` (or a reasonable limit) to the `operations` field.
- Add validation annotations to `SyncOperation` fields (`op`, `entity`, `id`).
- Return 400 Bad Request for invalid payloads.
- Add unit tests for validation constraints.

title: Add validation constraints to SyncOperation fields
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncOperation.java`, the fields `op`, `entity`, `id`, and `data` have no validation constraints. Any value is accepted.

### Impact
Invalid or malicious data can be persisted to the database. No enforcement of allowed operation types or entity names.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@NotBlank` to `op` and `entity` fields.
- Restrict `op` to an enum or pattern (`CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`).
- Restrict `entity` to known entity types (`student`, `custom_exercise`, `routine`, `assigned_routine`).
- Add `@Valid` to the operations list in `SyncPushRequest` to trigger cascading validation.

title: Implement input sanitization across all endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
User-supplied data from request bodies (student names, exercise names, descriptions, etc.) is stored directly in the database without sanitization across multiple files.

### Impact
If the data is later rendered in a frontend, stored XSS attacks become possible. Malicious HTML/JavaScript could be injected through any user input field.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a sanitization utility that strips HTML tags and dangerous characters.
- Apply sanitization to all string fields received from user input.
- Add tests verifying that malicious input is sanitized before persistence.

title: Remove anonymous.disable() from SecurityConfig
body:
### Current Issue
In `SecurityConfig.java` (line 42), `anonymous.disable()` prevents the anonymous user from having a principal in the security context.

### Impact
This can cause unexpected NullPointerExceptions in code that assumes `Authentication` is always non-null, and breaks the standard Spring Security anonymous handling.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Remove the `.anonymous(anonymous -> anonymous.disable())` line.
- Verify all endpoints still behave correctly for unauthenticated requests.
- Ensure the global exception handler catches any NPE from missing authentication.

title: Remove unused CustomExerciseResponse DTO class
body:
### Current Issue
`CustomExerciseResponse.java` exists but is never used. Controllers return `UnifiedExerciseResponse` instead. This is dead code that creates confusion.

### Impact
Developers may mistakenly use the wrong DTO, leading to inconsistent API responses. Dead code increases maintenance burden.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Delete `CustomExerciseResponse.java` and its import references.
- Verify the project compiles and all tests pass.
- Confirm no reflection-based code references the deleted class.

title: Wrap SyncService.push() operations in a transaction
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncService.java`, the `push()` method executes each operation independently. If operation 3 of 5 fails, operations 1-2 are persisted while 3-5 are not. There is no rollback or consistency guarantee.

### Impact
Partial sync states leave the client and server out of sync. The client receives a mixed success/error response with no clear retry strategy.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Wrap the entire `push()` method in a `@Transactional` annotation.
- On any failure, roll back all operations (all-or-nothing).
- Return clear error messaging indicating the entire batch failed.
- Add integration tests verifying transaction rollback on failure.

title: Return structured error response instead of partial errors from sync push
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncService.java` (line 48), the `push()` method catches exceptions per operation and returns them as part of the response. The client has no clear indication of whether to retry or not.

### Impact
Clients cannot reliably determine the state of their data. Partial failures may lead to data corruption on retry.

### Acceptance Criteria
- After implementing all-or-nothing transactions (see previous issue), return a single success/error status for the batch.
- On error, return the specific error message and failed operation details.
- Document the retry strategy for clients.

title: Replace JPA entity leakage in SyncPullResponse with DTOs
body:
### Current Issue
`SyncPullResponse` returns `List<Student>` (raw JPA entity) as HTTP response. This triggers lazy initialization exceptions and exposes the internal data model including foreign keys.

### Impact
Lazy loading exceptions can crash the response. Internal field names and relationships are exposed to API consumers.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a `StudentSyncDto` with only the fields needed by clients.
- Map Student entities to DTOs in `SyncService.pull()`.
- Ensure no lazy-loaded associations are accessed during serialization.
- Verify the API response matches the documented contract.

title: Refactor RoutineService.update() to preserve entity IDs
body:
### Current Issue
In `RoutineService.java` (line 68), the `update()` method deletes all RoutineDay children and recreates them from scratch, losing the original database IDs.

### Impact
Any external references to those IDs (assigned routines, client bookmarks, shared links) become broken after an update.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Implement a diff-based update strategy: update existing days, add new ones, remove deleted ones.
- Preserve database IDs for days, blocks, and sub-exercises that are not deleted.
- Add integration tests verifying ID preservation across updates.
- Ensure orphan removal still works for explicitly deleted children.

title: Inject Spring-managed ObjectMapper in SeedRunner and AiService
body:
### Current Issue
Both `SeedRunner.java` and `AiService.java` create `new ObjectMapper()` instances instead of injecting the Spring-managed bean configured in `JacksonConfig`. Custom Jackson configurations (e.g., `JavaTimeModule`) are lost.

### Impact
Date serialization/deserialization may behave inconsistently. Configuration applied in `JacksonConfig` is ignored by these classes.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Inject `ObjectMapper` via constructor in `SeedRunner` and `AiService`.
- Remove all `new ObjectMapper()` calls from these classes.
- Verify all Jackson configuration from `JacksonConfig` is applied.
- Run existing tests to confirm no regressions.

title: Add SLF4J logging to all service classes
body:
### Current Issue
There are zero `Logger` instances across the entire application. All files lack any form of structured logging.

### Impact
It is impossible to diagnose issues in production. There is no visibility into request processing, error conditions, or performance bottlenecks.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ClassName.class)` to all service and controller classes.
- Log key events: method entry/exit for write operations, error conditions with stack traces, security events (login attempts, access denials).
- Ensure log levels are appropriate (INFO for business events, WARN for recoverable errors, ERROR for failures).
- Verify logging does not expose sensitive data (passwords, tokens).

title: Replace generic exceptions with domain-specific exception classes
body:
### Current Issue
`IllegalArgumentException` is used across multiple services to signal business errors, authentication errors, and validation errors. The `GlobalExceptionHandler` cannot distinguish between them.

### Impact
All `IllegalArgumentException` responses return 400 Bad Request, even when 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden would be appropriate. Error responses are misleading.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create domain-specific exceptions: `TrainerNotFoundException`, `StudentNotFoundException`, `OwnershipViolationException`, etc.
- Update `GlobalExceptionHandler` to map each exception to the correct HTTP status.
- Replace all `IllegalArgumentException` throws in services with the appropriate domain exception.
- Add tests verifying correct HTTP status codes for each exception type.

title: Extract common trainer lookup into a shared service or helper
body:
### Current Issue
Every service (StudentService, RoutineService, CustomExerciseService, AssignedRoutineService, ExerciseService, SyncService) independently calls `trainerRepository.findByEmail()` and throws `IllegalArgumentException("Entrenador no encontrado")`. This pattern is repeated in 8+ places.

### Impact
Code duplication makes maintenance error-prone. Changing the lookup logic or error message requires updating every service.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a `TrainerContext` service or utility that encapsulates the email-to-Trainer resolution.
- Inject and use this helper in all services that need the current trainer.
- Ensure error handling is centralized and consistent.
- Verify all existing tests still pass.

title: Replace SeedRunner with Flyway or Liquibase migrations
body:
### Current Issue
`SeedRunner.java` is a `CommandLineRunner` that executes on every application startup. It seeds exercise data from a JSON file if the table is empty.

### Impact
Running seed logic on every startup is fragile. It cannot handle schema evolution, is not idempotent, and mixes seed data with application lifecycle.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add Flyway or Liquibase dependency to `pom.xml`.
- Create a migration script that seeds the exercise data as an INSERT statement.
- Remove the `SeedRunner` class.
- Verify the seed data is applied correctly on a fresh database.
- Ensure subsequent startups do not duplicate data.

title: Configure timeouts on RestTemplate bean
body:
### Current Issue
In `WebConfig.java`, the `RestTemplate` bean is created without any timeout configuration. If the Gemini API is slow or unresponsive, the calling thread blocks indefinitely.

### Impact
Thread pool exhaustion under load. A single slow external API call can cascade into application-wide unresponsiveness.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Configure `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` on the `RestTemplate` (e.g., 5 seconds connect, 30 seconds read).
- Add error handling for timeout scenarios in `AiService`.
- Log timeout events for monitoring.
- Add tests simulating slow external responses.

title: Remove custom JacksonConfig ObjectMapper bean override
body:
### Current Issue
`JacksonConfig.java` creates a new `ObjectMapper` bean that overrides Spring Boot's auto-configured one, losing built-in configurations like `JavaTimeModule` for `LocalDateTime` serialization.

### Impact
`LocalDateTime` fields in API responses may serialize incorrectly (e.g., as arrays instead of ISO strings). Other auto-configured features are lost.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Delete `JacksonConfig.java` entirely, or configure it to extend the default ObjectMapper (e.g., `@Bean public ObjectMapper objectMapper(ObjectMapperBuilder builder)`).
- Verify `LocalDateTime` serialization works correctly in all API responses.
- Run the full test suite to confirm no regressions.

title: Standardize DTO pattern: prefer records over mutable classes
body:
### Current Issue
The project mixes DTO patterns: some DTOs are Java records (e.g., `AuthResponse`, `ShareResponse`), while others are mutable classes with getters/setters (e.g., `RoutineResponse`, `AssignedRoutineResponse`). There is no clear convention.

### Impact
Inconsistent code style reduces readability and increases cognitive load for developers.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Choose a single DTO pattern (records recommended for immutability).
- Refactor all mutable DTOs to records (or vice versa, depending on team decision).
- Update all mapping code that calls setters.
- Verify all tests pass after refactoring.

title: Add API versioning prefix (e.g., /api/v1/)
body:
### Current Issue
There is no API versioning strategy. All endpoints are served under the context path `/api` without a version prefix. Breaking changes will immediately affect all clients.

### Impact
Client applications cannot be migrated gradually. Any API change is a breaking change for all consumers.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a version prefix (e.g., `/api/v1/`) to all controller mappings.
- Ensure the old context path still works via a redirect or alias during migration.
- Document the versioning strategy.
- Update API specification documents.

title: Refactor RoutineService to remove direct EntityManager usage
body:
### Current Issue
`RoutineService.java` uses `@PersistenceContext EntityManager` directly alongside Spring Data repositories for removing days. This mixes two persistence access patterns inconsistently.

### Impact
Direct EntityManager usage bypasses Spring Data's abstraction layer, making the code harder to test and maintain.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Remove the `EntityManager` dependency from `RoutineService`.
- Use only Spring Data repositories for all persistence operations.
- Rely on `CascadeType.ALL` and `orphanRemoval` for child entity cleanup.
- Verify all CRUD operations and cascade behaviors still work correctly.

title: Extract RoutineService.toResponse() mapping to MapStruct
body:
### Current Issue
In `RoutineService.java` (line 110), the `toResponse()` method has 50+ lines of manual mapping code converting entities to DTOs.

### Impact
Manual mapping is error-prone and verbose. Adding new fields requires updating the mapping in multiple places.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add MapStruct dependency to `pom.xml`.
- Create a `RoutineMapper` interface with `@Mapper` annotation.
- Replace the manual mapping with generated mapper calls.
- Verify all routine-related tests pass with the new mapper.
- Delete the manual `toResponse()` method.

title: Log serialization failures in CustomExerciseService.toJson()
body:
### Current Issue
In `CustomExerciseService.java` (line 107), the `toJson()` method catches `JsonProcessingException` and silently returns `"[]"`. The lost data is never reported.

### Impact
Data is silently lost without any trace in logs. Debugging why an exercise has empty secondary muscles becomes very difficult.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a `log.error()` call with the exception details when serialization fails.
- Throw a runtime exception or return a clear error to the caller instead of silently returning `"[]"`.
- Add tests verifying the error handling behavior.

title: Remove unused joinListPipe() method from SeedRunner
body:
### Current Issue
In `SeedRunner.java` (line 54), the private method `joinListPipe()` is never called from anywhere in the codebase.

### Impact
Dead code increases maintenance burden and can confuse developers about its intended purpose.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Delete the `joinListPipe()` method.
- Verify the project compiles and all tests pass.
- Search for any reflection-based references to confirm it is safe to remove.

title: Change ddl-auto from 'update' to 'validate' in production
body:
### Current Issue
In `application.yml` (line 11), `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` is set to `update`. Hibernate can modify the production database schema automatically.

### Impact
Automatic schema changes in production can cause data loss, index corruption, or unexpected column additions. This is explicitly warned against in Hibernate documentation.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Change `ddl-auto` to `validate` in `application.yml`.
- Create an `application-prod.yml` with `ddl-auto: validate`.
- Add Flyway/Liquibase for explicit schema migrations.
- Verify the application starts correctly against the current schema.

title: Normalize CSV fields in Exercise table to proper relational storage
body:
### Current Issue
In `Exercise.java`, the fields `targetMuscles`, `bodyParts`, `equipments`, and `secondaryMuscles` store multiple values as comma-separated strings in a single column.

### Impact
This violates First Normal Form (1NF). It is impossible to perform efficient joins, enforce referential integrity, or query by individual muscle/equipment. LIKE queries with leading wildcards cannot use indexes.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create junction tables: `exercise_muscles`, `exercise_body_parts`, `exercise_equipments`, `exercise_secondary_muscles`.
- Create a Flyway migration to transform existing CSV data into relational rows.
- Update `ExerciseRepository` queries to use JOINs instead of LIKE.
- Update `ExerciseService` and DTOs to work with the new schema.
- Verify all exercise-related tests pass.

title: Standardize list storage format across all entities
body:
### Current Issue
Three different formats are used for storing lists: `Exercise.instructions` uses JSONB, `SubExerciseDetail.instructions` uses pipe-separated via `StringListConverter`, and `CustomExercise.secondaryMuscles` uses a JSON string.

### Impact
Inconsistent storage makes queries unpredictable, parsing logic fragile, and data migration difficult.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Choose a single format (JSONB recommended for PostgreSQL).
- Create migrations to convert pipe-separated and JSON string columns to JSONB.
- Replace `StringListConverter` with JSONB column type.
- Update all entity mappings and query code accordingly.

title: Replace AssignedBlock JSON snapshot with relational references
body:
### Current Issue
In `AssignedBlock.java`, `blockData` stores the entire exercise block as a serialized JSON string. This is a snapshot of the template at assignment time.

### Impact
If the routine template is modified, the assigned routine becomes stale with no way to synchronize. The JSON blob cannot be queried or indexed.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Design a proper relational model for assigned blocks (referencing exercise IDs, sets, reps, etc.).
- Create a migration to convert existing JSON data to relational rows.
- Update `AssignedRoutineService` serialization/deserialization logic.
- Ensure assigned routines can optionally sync with template changes.
- Verify all assigned routine tests pass.

title: Add foreign key constraints for exercise and day references
body:
### Current Issue
In `SubExerciseDetail.java`, `exerciseId` is a plain String with no foreign key to the `exercises` table. In `AssignedRoutineDay.java`, `dayId` references `RoutineDay` without a FK constraint.

### Impact
Deleting an exercise or routine day leaves orphaned references. Database integrity cannot be enforced at the schema level.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a foreign key from `sub_exercise_details.exercise_id` to `exercises.id` (or document why it is intentionally loose for snapshots).
- Add a foreign key from `assigned_routine_days.day_id` to `routine_days.id` (if appropriate for the snapshot model).
- Create a migration script for the constraints.
- Verify no orphaned records exist before applying constraints.

title: Add database indexes on frequently queried columns
body:
### Current Issue
Multiple repository methods (`findByTrainerId()`, `findByStudentId()`, `findByShareUrl()`) query by columns that have no declared indexes.

### Impact
As data grows, these queries will degrade to full table scans. Share URL lookups (which are unauthenticated) will become particularly slow.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add indexes on: `students.trainer_id`, `routines.trainer_id`, `custom_exercises.trainer_id`, `assigned_routines.trainer_id`, `assigned_routines.student_id`, `assigned_routines.share_url`.
- Create a Flyway migration for the indexes.
- Verify query performance with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on sample data.
- Ensure index creation does not lock tables in production.

title: Add database integrity constraints (unique, check, not-null)
body:
### Current Issue
Multiple entities lack important database constraints: no composite unique constraints, no check constraints (e.g., `age > 0`), and missing NOT NULL on important fields.

### Impact
Invalid data can be persisted (negative ages, duplicate entries for unique business keys). Data quality issues accumulate silently.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `CHECK (age > 0 AND age < 150)` constraint on students.age.
- Add composite unique constraints where business logic requires it.
- Audit all `nullable = false` annotations and add missing ones.
- Create a migration script for all new constraints.
- Verify existing data satisfies all new constraints before applying.

title: Replace LocalDateTime.now() with timezone-aware timestamps
body:
### Current Issue
All entities use `LocalDateTime.now()` in `@PrePersist` and `@PreUpdate` callbacks. `LocalDateTime` does not carry timezone information.

### Impact
In multi-timezone deployments or clusters, timestamps are inconsistent. Comparing timestamps across regions produces incorrect results.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Change all `LocalDateTime` fields to `Instant` or `OffsetDateTime`.
- Update `@PrePersist`/`@PreUpdate` to use `Instant.now()`.
- Create a migration to handle any existing data (if needed).
- Update all DTOs and API responses to use ISO-8601 format with timezone.
- Verify all date-related tests pass.

title: Implement soft deletes across all entities
body:
### Current Issue
All entities use hard deletes via `repository.delete()`. Once deleted, data cannot be recovered.

### Impact
Accidental deletes cause permanent data loss. There is no audit trail of deletions. Recovery from mistakes requires database restores.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a `deletedAt` (nullable `Instant`) column to all entities.
- Override `delete()` methods to set `deletedAt` instead of removing rows.
- Add `@Where(clause = "deleted_at IS NULL")` or equivalent to filter deleted records by default.
- Add an admin endpoint or scheduled job to purge soft-deleted records after a retention period.
- Update all queries to exclude soft-deleted records.

title: Add audit trail (createdBy/updatedBy) to all entities
body:
### Current Issue
All entities have `createdAt` and `updatedAt` fields but no `createdBy` or `updatedBy` fields. There is no record of which user made changes.

### Impact
It is impossible to attribute changes to specific users for compliance, debugging, or dispute resolution.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `createdBy` and `updatedBy` fields to all entities.
- Populate them automatically using the authenticated user from Spring Security context.
- Create a JPA auditing configuration with `@EnableJpaAuditing` and `AuditorAware`.
- Update DTOs to expose audit fields where appropriate.

title: Standardize column naming conventions across entities
body:
### Current Issue
Column naming is inconsistent: `disciplina` and `objetivos` are in Spanish while all other fields are in English. `is_combined` vs `isCustom` uses different conventions.

### Impact
Inconsistent naming makes the schema harder to understand and increases the chance of typos in queries.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Rename Spanish columns to English equivalents via a migration.
- Standardize boolean columns to use a consistent prefix (e.g., `is_` or none).
- Update all entity annotations, queries, and DTOs.
- Document the naming convention in the project README.

title: Review CascadeType.ALL usage on entity relationships
body:
### Current Issue
`Routine.java` uses `CascadeType.ALL` with `orphanRemoval = true` on the `days` collection, and this cascades deeply through `RoutineDay -> ExerciseBlock -> SubExerciseDetail`.

### Impact
Deleting or modifying a parent entity can silently delete deeply nested children. This aggressive cascade can cause unexpected data loss if not managed carefully.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Audit all `CascadeType.ALL` usages and narrow to specific cascade types (PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE as needed).
- Document the cascade behavior for each relationship.
- Ensure orphan removal only applies where logically required.
- Add integration tests verifying cascade behavior.

title: Configure HikariCP connection pool settings
body:
### Current Issue
`application.yml` has no HikariCP configuration. It relies entirely on Spring Boot defaults.

### Impact
Under high load, default pool sizes may be insufficient, causing connection timeouts and degraded performance.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Configure `spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size`, `minimum-idle`, and `connection-timeout` in `application.yml`.
- Add an `application-prod.yml` with production-tuned values.
- Document the rationale for chosen values.
- Monitor connection pool metrics after deployment.

title: Align Exercise.id generation strategy with other entities
body:
### Current Issue
In `Exercise.java`, the `@Id` field uses a manually assigned String ID from the seed data. All other entities use `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.UUID)`.

### Impact
Inconsistent ID generation makes the codebase harder to understand and complicates any future migration to a different ID strategy.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Evaluate whether Exercise IDs should switch to auto-generated UUIDs.
- If keeping manual IDs, document the rationale clearly in the entity.
- Ensure all foreign key references remain consistent.
- Update seed data if the ID strategy changes.

title: Add updated_at column to RoutineDay entity
body:
### Current Issue
`RoutineDay.java` only has a `created_at` column. There is no `updated_at` field to track modifications.

### Impact
It is impossible to determine when a routine day was last modified. This complicates sync logic and debugging.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@Column(name = "updated_at", nullable = false)` field to `RoutineDay`.
- Add `@PreUpdate` callback to set the timestamp.
- Create a migration to add the column with a default value.
- Verify all routine-related tests pass.

title: Use native JSONB for CustomExercise.secondaryMuscles
body:
### Current Issue
`CustomExercise.secondaryMuscles` stores JSON as a plain String column, while `Exercise.instructions` uses native JSONB with `@JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON)`.

### Impact
Plain JSON strings cannot be queried with PostgreSQL JSON operators. The inconsistency makes the schema harder to maintain.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Change the column type to JSONB via migration.
- Update the entity annotation to use `@JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON)`.
- Remove the manual JSON serialization in `CustomExerciseService.toJson()`.
- Verify all custom exercise tests pass.

title: Refactor RoutineRepository.delete() to handle deep cascade safely
body:
### Current Issue
`RoutineRepository` inherits `delete()` from `JpaRepository`. With deep cascades (Routine -> Day -> Block -> SubExercise), the delete may fail or behave unexpectedly depending on orphan removal configuration.

### Impact
Deleting a routine with deeply nested children may fail due to constraint violations or leave orphaned records.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a custom `@Modifying @Query` or use `deleteInBatch()` if appropriate.
- Verify all children are properly deleted via integration tests.
- Benchmark delete performance with large nested structures.

title: Extract duplicated routine-building logic in RoutineService
body:
### Current Issue
`RoutineService.java` has nearly identical code in `create()` (lines 30-60) and `update()` (lines 78-108) for building days, blocks, and sub-exercises from the request DTO.

### Impact
The ~50 lines of duplicated code means any bug fix or feature change must be applied in two places. This is error-prone and violates DRY.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Extract the common logic into a private method (e.g., `buildDaysFromRequest(CreateRoutineRequest, Routine)`).
- Call this method from both `create()` and `update()`.
- Verify all routine CRUD tests pass after refactoring.
- Add a comment explaining the shared logic.

title: Replace magic strings with constants or enum
body:
### Current Issue
Error message strings like "Entrenador no encontrado", "Alumno no encontrado", "Plantilla no pertenece a este entrenador" are repeated verbatim across 8+ service files.

### Impact
Typos in repeated strings cause silent bugs. Changing an error message requires updating multiple files. No single source of truth.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a `Messages` constants class or enum with all error messages.
- Replace all hardcoded strings with references to the constants.
- Ensure error messages remain in Spanish (matching current behavior) or migrate to i18n.
- Verify all tests that assert on error messages are updated.

title: Configure RestTemplate with timeouts and error handling
body:
### Current Issue
In `WebConfig.java`, the `RestTemplate` bean is created with zero configuration — no timeouts, no interceptors, no error handling.

### Impact
Unbounded request durations can exhaust thread pools. No retry logic for transient failures. No request/response logging for debugging.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Configure connect timeout (5s) and read timeout (30s) using `HttpComponentsClientHttpRequestFactory`.
- Add a `ClientHttpRequestInterceptor` for logging requests/responses.
- Implement error handling in `AiService` for timeout and 5xx responses.
- Add tests simulating slow and failing external services.

title: Fix JacksonConfig to not override Spring Boot's ObjectMapper
body:
### Current Issue
`JacksonConfig.java` creates a bare `new ObjectMapper()` bean, overriding Spring Boot's auto-configured ObjectMapper which includes `JavaTimeModule`, `Jdk8Module`, and other useful modules.

### Impact
`LocalDateTime` serialization breaks. Date fields in API responses may appear as arrays of numbers instead of ISO-8601 strings.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Delete `JacksonConfig.java` or refactor it to extend the auto-configured ObjectMapper.
- Verify `LocalDateTime` serialization in `RoutineResponse.createdAt` produces ISO-8601 strings.
- Run the full test suite.

title: Extract shared test SQL data into a common base script
body:
### Current Issue
The trainer INSERT statements are duplicated across `student-test-data.sql`, `custom-exercise-test-data.sql`, and `assigned-test-data.sql`.

### Impact
Updating test data requires editing 3 files. Inconsistencies between files can cause test failures.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a `common-test-data.sql` with shared trainer inserts.
- Reference it from other test SQL files using Spring's `@Sql` with multiple scripts.
- Remove duplicated INSERT statements from individual files.
- Verify all tests still pass.

title: Replace Java assert with JUnit Assertions in tests
body:
### Current Issue
In `StudentControllerTest.java` (line 68) and other test files, Java's `assert` keyword is used for test assertions instead of JUnit's `Assertions.assertEquals`.

### Impact
Java assertions can be disabled with the `-da` JVM flag. Tests would silently pass without actually verifying anything.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Replace all `assert` statements with `Assertions.assertEquals`, `Assertions.assertTrue`, etc.
- Add import for `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`.
- Verify all tests pass with assertions enabled.

title: Remove unused @JsonProperty annotations from CustomExerciseRequest
body:
### Current Issue
In `CustomExerciseRequest.java`, `@JsonProperty` annotations are used on record fields. Jackson already maps record component names correctly without explicit annotations.

### Impact
Redundant annotations add noise and suggest the naming requires manual override when it does not.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Remove all `@JsonProperty` annotations from `CustomExerciseRequest`.
- Verify serialization/deserialization still works correctly in tests.
- Document the convention: records do not need `@JsonProperty` unless names differ.

title: Remove dead code from SeedRunner and CustomExerciseResponse
body:
### Current Issue
`SeedRunner.joinListPipe()` (line 54) is a private method never called. `CustomExerciseResponse.java` is a full class that is never used (controllers use `UnifiedExerciseResponse`).

### Impact
Dead code increases cognitive load and maintenance burden. Developers may waste time understanding code that serves no purpose.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Delete `joinListPipe()` from `SeedRunner`.
- Delete `CustomExerciseResponse.java` entirely.
- Search for any reflection or configuration references to the deleted class.
- Verify the project compiles and all tests pass.

title: Move cleanKey() from ExerciseController to a utility class
body:
### Current Issue
In `ExerciseController.java` (line 39), the `cleanKey()` method contains presentation logic (lowercasing, replacing spaces, removing special characters) that does not belong in a controller.

### Impact
Controllers should only handle HTTP concerns. Business/presentation logic in controllers is hard to test and reuse.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a `KeyUtils` or `StringUtils` utility class.
- Move `cleanKey()` logic to the utility.
- Update `ExerciseController` to call the utility.
- Add unit tests for the utility method.

title: Add pagination to student, routine, and custom-exercise list endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
`GET /students`, `GET /routines`, and `GET /custom-exercises` return all records without pagination. Only `GET /exercises` supports pagination.

### Impact
With thousands of records, response payloads become very large, causing slow responses and high memory usage on both client and server.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `page` and `limit` query parameters to all list endpoints (default page=1, limit=30).
- Return a standard pagination response envelope with total count, total pages, and current page.
- Update clients to use paginated responses.
- Add tests verifying pagination behavior.

title: Standardize API response envelope across all endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
Exercise endpoints return `{success, metadata, data}`, while student and routine endpoints return raw arrays `[]`. There is no consistent response format.

### Impact
Clients must handle multiple response shapes. Error handling becomes inconsistent. API documentation is harder to maintain.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Define a standard response envelope (e.g., `{success: boolean, data: ..., error: ...}`).
- Update all endpoints to use the standard envelope.
- Update the API specification document.
- Verify all tests match the new response format.

title: Add batch size limit to sync push endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
`POST /sync/push` accepts an unbounded list of operations. An attacker can send thousands of operations in a single request.

### Impact
Large batches can cause memory exhaustion, long transaction times, and denial of service.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@Size(max = 100)` (or a reasonable limit) to the operations list in `SyncPushRequest`.
- Return 400 Bad Request when the limit is exceeded.
- Document the maximum batch size in the API specification.
- Add a test verifying the limit is enforced.

title: Set a reasonable default for sync pull timestamp
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncController.java`, if `lastSyncTimestamp` is not provided, the default is `LocalDateTime.MIN`, which returns ALL data for the trainer.

### Impact
First-time clients or clients that lose their sync state will download the entire dataset, which can be very large.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Return an error if `lastSyncTimestamp` is missing, requiring clients to explicitly request a full sync.
- Or set a reasonable default (e.g., last 30 days) and document the behavior.
- Add pagination to sync pull responses.
- Update API documentation.

title: Support partial updates for PUT /routines/{id}
body:
### Current Issue
`PUT /routines/{id}` requires the complete routine structure (all days, blocks, sub-exercises). It is not possible to update only the name or description.

### Impact
Clients must fetch the full routine, modify one field, and send the entire structure back. This is inefficient and error-prone.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Support PATCH semantics or make PUT fields optional (keep existing values for omitted fields).
- Document which fields can be partially updated.
- Add tests for partial update scenarios.

title: Add rate limit headers to API responses
body:
### Current Issue
No endpoints return `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Clients have no visibility into their rate limit status.

### Impact
Clients cannot implement backoff strategies or display rate limit information to users.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers to all responses.
- Update the rate limiter to track and expose these metrics.
- Document the headers in the API specification.

title: Implement soft delete for DELETE endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
All DELETE endpoints perform hard deletes. Once a student, routine, or exercise is deleted, it cannot be recovered.

### Impact
Accidental deletions cause permanent data loss. No undo capability for users.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Implement soft deletes (see database issue D10) at the entity level.
- Update DELETE endpoints to set `deletedAt` instead of removing rows.
- Add a query filter to exclude soft-deleted records from list/get endpoints.
- Provide an admin endpoint for permanent deletion if needed.

title: Add ETag/If-None-Match support for routine detail endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
`GET /routines/{id}` has no support for conditional requests via ETags or If-None-Match headers.

### Impact
Clients must download the full routine even if it has not changed, wasting bandwidth and increasing latency.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Generate an ETag based on the routine's `updatedAt` timestamp.
- Return `304 Not Modified` when the `If-None-Match` header matches.
- Add tests verifying conditional request behavior.

title: Add CAPTCHA to registration endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
`POST /auth/register` has no CAPTCHA or bot protection. Automated scripts can create unlimited accounts.

### Impact
Spam accounts, credential stuffing attacks, and resource abuse.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Integrate a CAPTCHA service (e.g., reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha).
- Validate the CAPTCHA token on the server before processing registration.
- Return 400 Bad Request for invalid/missing CAPTCHA tokens.
- Ensure the CAPTCHA does not block legitimate users.

title: Fix partial update behavior in PUT /assigned-routines/{id}
body:
### Current Issue
`PUT /assigned-routines/{id}` only updates `studentId` and `coachName`, ignoring all other fields in the request body.

### Impact
Clients expect a full replacement semantics for PUT but get partial update behavior. This violates HTTP semantics and confuses API consumers.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Either implement full replacement (PUT) or rename to PATCH for partial updates.
- Update all mutable fields from the request body.
- Document the actual behavior in the API specification.
- Add tests for both full and partial update scenarios.

title: Add unit tests for service classes
body:
### Current Issue
All existing tests are integration tests requiring Testcontainers and a running database. There are zero unit tests for any service class.

### Impact
Unit tests are fast, isolated, and cheap to run. Without them, developers avoid running tests during development, leading to more bugs.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create unit tests for `AuthService`, `StudentService`, `RoutineService`, `ExerciseService`, `CustomExerciseService`, `AssignedRoutineService`.
- Mock all repository dependencies using Mockito.
- Test all business logic branches (happy path, not found, ownership violation, validation errors).
- Achieve at least 80% line coverage for service classes.

title: Add integration tests for SyncService endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
There are no tests for the `/sync/push` and `/sync/pull` endpoints. The sync feature is completely untested.

### Impact
Regression bugs in the sync logic can go undetected, potentially causing data loss or corruption for clients.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create `SyncControllerTest` with integration tests.
- Test push: create, update, delete operations for all entity types.
- Test pull: verify correct data is returned based on `lastSyncTimestamp`.
- Test error handling: invalid operations, unknown entities, ownership violations.
- Test batch size limits.

title: Replace hardcoded UUIDs in test data with dynamic generation
body:
### Current Issue
Test SQL files use hardcoded UUIDs like `aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa`. These are fragile and make tests hard to maintain.

### Impact
Tests depend on specific ID values. Changing the ID generation strategy breaks all tests. Developers must memorize ID patterns.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Generate test entities programmatically in `@BeforeEach` methods instead of SQL inserts.
- Use repository methods to create and retrieve test data.
- Remove hardcoded UUIDs from SQL files.
- Verify all tests pass with dynamic IDs.

title: Add comprehensive security integration tests
body:
### Current Issue
`AuthIntegrationTest.java` only verifies 401 without a token. It does not test: expired tokens, invalid tokens, role-based access, resource-level authorization.

### Impact
Security regressions can go undetected. Authorization bypasses may be introduced without triggering test failures.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add tests for expired JWT tokens (return 401).
- Add tests for malformed JWT tokens (return 401).
- Add tests verifying trainer A cannot access trainer B's resources (students, routines, assigned routines).
- Add tests for the shared routine endpoint (unauthenticated access).
- Add tests for rate limiting behavior.

title: Add edge case tests for input validation
body:
### Current Issue
No tests exist for edge cases such as extremely long input strings, special characters, Unicode, empty nested collections, or concurrent modifications.

### Impact
Input validation gaps can lead to data corruption, application crashes, or security vulnerabilities.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add tests for maximum-length strings in all text fields.
- Add tests for special characters and Unicode in user input.
- Add tests for empty and null nested collections.
- Add tests for concurrent modifications to the same resource.
- Document any edge cases that require special handling.

title: Change test ddl-auto from 'create-drop' to match production
body:
### Current Issue
In `application-test.yml` (line 11), `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` is set to `create-drop`, which does not reflect the production schema.

### Impact
Tests may pass against a schema that differs from production, hiding migration bugs or schema incompatibilities.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Change `ddl-auto` to `validate` in `application-test.yml`.
- Ensure test database is provisioned with the same migrations used in production.
- Verify all tests pass against the validated schema.

title: Add concurrency tests for RateLimiterService
body:
### Current Issue
`RateLimiterService` uses `ConcurrentHashMap` and `synchronized` blocks but has no tests verifying thread-safety under concurrent access.

### Impact
Race conditions could allow more requests than the configured limit, or cause exceptions under load.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create a concurrent test that sends N requests from M threads simultaneously.
- Verify the rate limit is enforced correctly under contention.
- Verify no `ConcurrentModificationException` or data corruption occurs.
- Use `CountDownLatch` or similar for synchronization.

title: Add load and stress tests for critical endpoints
body:
### Current Issue
There are no load tests or stress tests for any endpoint. Performance characteristics under load are unknown.

### Impact
Production incidents caused by unexpected load go undetected until users report them.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Set up a load testing tool (e.g., Gatling, JMeter, k6).
- Create load test scripts for: `/auth/login`, `/exercises`, `/routines`, `/sync/push`.
- Define performance baselines (e.g., p95 response time < 500ms).
- Run load tests in CI and fail on regression.

title: Add .dockerignore file
body:
### Current Issue
There is no `.dockerignore` file. The `COPY` instructions in the Dockerfile copy everything, including `target/`, `.idea/`, `.git/`, `node_modules/`, and other unnecessary files.

### Impact
Docker image build context is unnecessarily large, slowing down builds and increasing image size.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create `.dockerignore` excluding: `.git/`, `.idea/`, `target/`, `*.log`, `.env`, `.env.local`, `node_modules/`, `*.iml`.
- Verify the Docker build context size is reduced.
- Verify the application still builds and runs correctly in Docker.

title: Switch Dockerfile runtime image from JDK to JRE
body:
### Current Issue
In `Dockerfile` (line 11), the runtime stage uses `eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine`. A JDK includes development tools not needed at runtime.

### Impact
The production image is significantly larger than necessary (JDK ~300MB vs JRE ~100MB). Larger images mean slower pulls and more attack surface.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Change the base image to `eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine`.
- Verify the application starts and runs correctly.
- Measure and document the image size reduction.

title: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction to Dockerfile
body:
### Current Issue
The `Dockerfile` has no `HEALTHCHECK` instruction. Docker and Kubernetes cannot determine if the application is actually healthy.

### Impact
Orchestrators may route traffic to unhealthy containers. Failed health checks are not detected automatically.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add a `HEALTHCHECK` instruction using `curl` to the actuator health endpoint (once Actuator is added).
- Set appropriate intervals and timeouts.
- Verify Docker reports container health status correctly.

title: Optimize Dockerfile with dependency caching
body:
### Current Issue
In `Dockerfile` (line 5), `COPY pom.xml .` and `COPY src ./src` are separate layers, but Maven dependencies are not cached between builds.

### Impact
Every code change triggers a full Maven dependency download, significantly slowing down builds.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Copy `pom.xml` first, run `mvn dependency:go-offline`, then copy `src/`.
- Verify subsequent builds with only source changes skip dependency download.
- Document the build time improvement.

title: Add Spring Boot Actuator for health and metrics
body:
### Current Issue
There is no Spring Boot Actuator dependency. The application has no health check endpoints, metrics, or operational information.

### Impact
It is impossible to monitor the application's health, track performance metrics, or integrate with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana).

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `spring-boot-starter-actuator` dependency to `pom.xml`.
- Expose `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/info` endpoints.
- Configure Actuator to not expose sensitive endpoints by default.
- Integrate with Docker HEALTHCHECK.
- Document available endpoints.

title: Create application-prod.yml with production-safe configuration
body:
### Current Issue
Only `application.yml` and `application-test.yml` exist. There is no `application-prod.yml` with secure defaults for production deployment.

### Impact
Production deployments may use development defaults (e.g., verbose logging, permissive CORS, debug endpoints).

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create `application-prod.yml` with: `ddl-auto: validate`, restricted CORS, minimal logging, Actuator exposure limited to health/info.
- Ensure all secrets come from environment variables with no defaults.
- Document the production configuration in deployment docs.

title: Document required environment variables
body:
### Current Issue
There is no `.env.example` or documentation listing the required environment variables (`JWT_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `PORT`).

### Impact
New developers and deployers must read the source code to discover required configuration. Misconfigurations are common.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Create `.env.example` with all required variables and placeholder values.
- Add a section in the project README explaining each variable.
- Ensure the application fails fast with a clear error if any variable is missing.

title: Add healthcheck to docker-compose postgres service
body:
### Current Issue
In `docker-compose.yml`, the `postgres` service has no `healthcheck` configuration. The application may start before the database is ready.

### Impact
The Spring Boot application may fail to connect to the database on startup, causing crash loops.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `healthcheck` with `pg_isready` command to the postgres service.
- Add `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` to the application service.
- Verify the application waits for the database to be ready.

title: Add restart policy to docker-compose services
body:
### Current Issue
`docker-compose.yml` has no `restart` policy. If a service crashes, it stays down.

### Impact
Manual intervention is required to restart crashed services, increasing downtime.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `restart: unless-stopped` to all services.
- Verify services restart automatically after `docker compose stop` and `docker compose start`.
- Test crash recovery by killing a process manually.

title: Add network isolation to docker-compose
body:
### Current Issue
All services in `docker-compose.yml` are on the default network. There is no isolation between services.

### Impact
All containers can communicate with each other, increasing the attack surface if one container is compromised.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Define explicit networks (e.g., `frontend`, `backend`).
- Place the application and postgres on the backend network only.
- Verify the application can reach postgres but not external services directly.

title: Add resource limits to docker-compose services
body:
### Current Issue
`docker-compose.yml` has no `deploy.resources.limits` configured for CPU or memory.

### Impact
A memory leak in the application can consume all host resources, causing the entire system to fail.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Set memory limits (e.g., `512m` for app, `256m` for postgres).
- Set CPU limits (e.g., `0.5` cores).
- Monitor resource usage to tune limits appropriately.
- Verify the application functions within the set limits.

title: Fix N+1 query problem in RoutineService.toResponse()
body:
### Current Issue
In `RoutineService.java` (line 110), the `toResponse()` method lazy-loads `days`, then `blocks`, then `subExercises` in a cascading manner. Each level triggers a separate SQL query.

### Impact
A routine with 3 days, 5 blocks per day, and 2 exercises per block generates 1 + 3 + 15 + 30 = 49 SQL queries instead of 1-2.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@EntityGraph` or `JOIN FETCH` to the `findByTrainerId()` and `findById()` queries.
- Verify the query count is reduced to 1-2 queries using Hibernate SQL logging.
- Benchmark response time before and after the fix.
- Ensure all routine tests pass.

title: Replace leading-wildcard LIKE queries with full-text search
body:
### Current Issue
In `ExerciseRepository.java` (line 10), the search query uses `LIKE '%query%'` which cannot use standard B-tree indexes in PostgreSQL.

### Impact
With thousands of exercises, every search performs a full table scan (O(n) complexity).

### Acceptance Criteria
- Implement PostgreSQL full-text search using `tsvector` and `tsquery`.
- Create a GIN index on the `name_normalized` column.
- Update the repository query to use `@@` full-text search operator.
- Verify search performance with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
- Maintain backward compatibility with the existing API contract.

title: Fix findDistinctTargetMuscles to return actual distinct values
body:
### Current Issue
In `ExerciseRepository.java` (line 21), `findDistinctTargetMuscles()` returns `DISTINCT e.targetMuscles`, but `targetMuscles` is a CSV string. This returns unique CSV strings, not individual muscle values.

### Impact
The muscles dropdown shows combined strings like "Pecho,Tríceps" instead of individual values like "Pecho", "Tríceps".

### Acceptance Criteria
- If CSV columns are normalized to relational tables (see D2), query the junction table directly.
- If keeping CSV temporarily, use PostgreSQL `unnest(string_to_array(...))` to split and distinct.
- Return a sorted list of individual muscle/equipment values.

title: Add pagination to sync pull endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
In `SyncService.java` (line 60), the `pull()` method returns all modified records since a timestamp with no pagination or limit.

### Impact
A trainer with thousands of students, routines, and assignments will receive an extremely large response, potentially causing timeouts or memory issues.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `page` and `limit` parameters to the pull endpoint.
- Return a `nextPageToken` or cursor for fetching subsequent pages.
- Set a maximum page size (e.g., 100 records per entity type).
- Document the pagination behavior in the API specification.

title: Add caching for exercise catalog data
body:
### Current Issue
There are no `@Cacheable` annotations anywhere in the application. Exercise catalog data (which is essentially static) is queried from the database on every request.

### Impact
Repeated requests for the exercise list generate unnecessary database load. Response times are higher than necessary.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `spring-boot-starter-cache` and a cache provider (e.g., Caffeine).
- Add `@Cacheable` to `ExerciseRepository` queries and `ExerciseService` methods.
- Implement cache eviction when exercises are seeded or updated.
- Verify cache hit rates using Actuator metrics.
- Benchmark response time improvement.

title: Make RateLimiterService distributed using Redis
body:
### Current Issue
`RateLimiterService` stores rate limit data in a `ConcurrentHashMap` on a single JVM instance. In a multi-instance deployment, each instance has its own counter.

### Impact
Rate limits are not enforced across instances. An attacker can send N * maxRequests requests by hitting different instances.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add Spring Data Redis dependency.
- Implement a Redis-based sliding window rate limiter.
- Configure Redis connection in `application.yml`.
- Verify rate limits are enforced across multiple application instances.
- Add tests simulating distributed rate limiting.

title: Inject ObjectMapper in AiService instead of creating new instance
body:
### Current Issue
In `AiService.java` (line 57), `parseExercise()` creates `new ObjectMapper()` on every call instead of using the Spring-managed bean.

### Impact
Each call creates a new ObjectMapper instance, which is expensive and loses any configured modules or customizations.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Inject `ObjectMapper` via constructor.
- Remove the `new ObjectMapper()` call.
- Verify the injected ObjectMapper has the correct configuration.
- Add a performance test measuring serialization throughput.

title: Configure HikariCP connection pool for production workloads
body:
### Current Issue
`application.yml` has no HikariCP configuration. Default pool size (10) may be insufficient for production traffic.

### Impact
Under load, the application may exhaust the connection pool, causing request timeouts and errors.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Configure `maximum-pool-size` based on expected load (e.g., 20-50).
- Configure `minimum-idle` to maintain warm connections.
- Configure `connection-timeout` to fail fast when pool is exhausted.
- Monitor pool metrics via Actuator.
- Document the configuration rationale.

title: Add HTTP connection pooling to RestTemplate
body:
### Current Issue
In `WebConfig.java`, `RestTemplate` is created without explicit HTTP client configuration. Depending on the default, each request may create a new HTTP connection.

### Impact
High-frequency calls to the Gemini API create and destroy TCP connections repeatedly, adding latency and resource overhead.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Configure `HttpComponentsClientHttpRequestFactory` with connection pooling.
- Set `maxTotal` and `defaultMaxPerRoute` connections.
- Configure connection time-to-live.
- Verify connection reuse with logging.

title: Fix N+1 query in StudentService list endpoint
body:
### Current Issue
In `StudentService.java` (line 33), `findByTrainerId()` returns students with `trainer` mapped as LAZY. If the controller or serialization accesses the trainer, it triggers N+1 queries.

### Impact
Listing students generates 1 + N queries (one per student) to load the trainer association.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"trainer"})` to `findByTrainerId()`.
- Or use a JPQL `JOIN FETCH` query.
- Verify the query count is reduced to 1.
- Ensure the trainer is not serialized in the student response (already marked `@JsonIgnore`).
